name: TITUS
full_name: Tokai Intermediate Tank for the Unoscillated Spectrum
summary: TITUS was a proposed gadolinium-loaded water-Cherenkov intermediate detector for the J-PARC to Hyper-Kamiokande programme. Its concept combined neutron tagging with magnetic muon measurement to reduce flux and interaction uncertainties.
physics_targets: Neutrino flux and neutrino-water interaction constraints for Hyper-Kamiokande
Supernova and other non-beam neutrino searches
detection_principle: A water-Cherenkov tank would reconstruct charged leptons from neutrino interactions, with gadolinium enhancing delayed-neutron capture signals. A magnetized muon-range detector would provide momentum and charge information for tracks leaving the tank.

sites.name: Proposed J-PARC intermediate-detector site
sites.location: Tokai, Ibaraki; approximately 2 km from the neutrino target

status.label: Proposed
status.evidence: The cited TITUS publications describe a proposal. A separate TITUS-named liquid-argon event-display software package is unrelated; the current IWCD is recorded as part of Hyper-Kamiokande.

timeline.event: Detailed design and projected physics reach released.

collaboration.name: TITUS Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.value: Approximately 2 km from the J-PARC neutrino target

key_parameters.name: Gadolinium concept
key_parameters.value: Approximately 0.1% loading for neutron tagging in the proposal

results.summary: Reported simulated reduction of Hyper-Kamiokande systematic uncertainties and other sensitivity projections; no TITUS neutrino data are reported.

science_scope: This dossier preserves a named historical proposal. Design parameters and sensitivity estimates are not measured neutrino results; later programmes using the same laboratory or technology are distinct.
